mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST declined by more than 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable economic environment conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 jobs in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is above 2% over the last quarter, it signals an accommodative monetary policy combined with strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was below 1% and GDPC1 growth was above 2% over the last quarter.
